title: Prop 2(ii)/deflation: (O3) excludes user-indexing, not the deflationist's actual thesis

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
The 𝓕∖𝓞_Φ witness Π_par has output 'depending on the user's community,' violating (O3). But the deflationist does not claim warrant depends on which *individual user* applies Π (a strawman); the claim is that warrant for a *fixed* procedure is constituted by community endorsement of that procedure. A community-endorsed but user-invariant procedure (e.g. 'accept h iff the standard textbook test passes') is NOT excluded by (O3) and could lie in 𝓕∩𝓞_Φ.

So the four-cell argument shows 𝓞_Φ ≠ 𝓕 as sets of formal objects, but not that objectivity-as-defined is not *constituted by* facts about practice — which (a) and the deflation rebuttal require. The slide from '(O3) excludes user-indexing' to 'objectivity is endorsement-independent' is unjustified.

Fix: rebuild the cell with a user-invariant but community-endorsed procedure that fails an *endorsement-independent* 𝓜 (see the endorsement-independence definition needed in the related issue).
